avg/recall: The log trick: the gradient of pi is pi times the gradient of ln pi. For fifty six, zero point two five is zero point five times zero point five.
avg/avg: The gradient of the expected reward, J, takes each answer's R times the gradient of its pi. Put the trick in, and each answer brings R times the gradient of ln pi, weighted by its probability. For seven times eight: zero point five times one, times the gradient for fifty six, plus zero point three times zero, plus zero point two times zero.
avg/draws: A real model has far too many answers to list. But drawing answers weights them for free: fifty six turns up in half the draws. So R times the gradient of ln pi, averaged over answers drawn from the model, written y drawn from pi, is the gradient of J.
avg/est: Even one draw gives an estimate of it: the sampled answer's reward, times the gradient of its log-probability. That estimate is the policy gradient.
avg/eg: For fifty six, this model's gradient of ln pi is zero point five, minus zero point three, minus zero point two. With R equal to one, the estimate is that same vector.
push/up: Step theta a little along the estimate, and the log-probability of the sampled answer rises, in proportion to R. A rewarded fifty six becomes more likely.
push/zero: A wrong answer gets R of zero, so its estimate is zero, and nothing moves.
push/neg: A negative reward flips the step, and makes that answer less likely.
push/loss: As a loss to minimize, it is minus R times log pi of the sample: cross-entropy on the model's own answer, weighted by its reward.
push/p1: Try one. A checker gives minus one for a wrong answer, and the model samples fifty four. Its gradient of ln pi is minus zero point five, zero point seven, minus zero point two. What is the estimate?
push/a1: Multiply each entry by R. Minus one flips every sign: zero point five, minus zero point seven, zero point two. It points where fifty four gets less likely.
push/p2: Now average it with a second sample: fifty six, with R of one, whose estimate is zero point five, minus zero point three, minus zero point two.
push/a2: Add the two entry by entry: one, minus one, and zero. Then halve: zero point five, minus zero point five, and zero.
